blockNote: Per-scene thinker spawn lists (Bank 0C, 845285-846683 = $0C:E5E5): a 256-word pointer table indexed by scene ID x 2 ($0646), followed by 70 lists of thinker-spawn records (204 records in all). SpawnSceneThinkers (thinker_execution) runs once per scene build: it reads scene_thinkers[$0646], allocates a thinker slot for every record up to the $FF terminator and calls InitThinkerFromSceneData. A zero pointer or a first byte with bit 7 set means no thinkers. The old note ('background AI thinkers: palette cyclers, HDMA effects, ambient handlers') was only half right: global_ambient_dispatcher, which 59 of the 70 lists contain, is the player palette and the talk interaction, not an ambient effect.
=== RECORD (4 bytes, extraction: thinker-spawn < param, @code >) ===
| Byte | Field |

| +0 | Spawn parameter: stored as animScratch+2 ($7F0002,X) of the new thinker. What it means is up to the code: the palette bundle ID for ambient_palette_cycler, the parallax_scroll_table index ($00-$24) for scanline_band_hdma_thinker, unused ($00) for most others |
| +1..+3 | Long pointer to the thinker's code; its first word becomes the thinker's filter flags (animScratch2) and the entry point is code + 2 |
A list ends with a $FF byte (bit 7 of byte 0 is the test), which the extraction does not print.
=== SHARING ===

- 70 of the 256 scenes use the bare list thinker_spawn_0CE7E5 (only global_ambient_dispatcher). Three more lists hold the same single record (0CE8E1 for scene $40, 0CE8EF and 0CE8F4 for scenes $4B and $4C).

- 43 scenes point at thinker_spawn_0CE7EA+8: the table entry may point into the middle of another scene's list, so a scene starts at a later record. The offset is in hex and counts bytes (4 per record): +4 skips one record, +8 two. 0CE7EA holds ambient_palette_cycler ($3F), flag_gated_palette_cool, scanline_band_hdma_thinker ($02) and global_ambient_dispatcher, so +8 = scanline band $02 plus the dispatcher. Two scenes ($04, $07) enter it at +0 and 4 at +4. The other shifted entries: 0CE80C+4, 0CE843+4 (2), 0CE861+8 (4), 0CE87F+4, 0CE8A1+8, 0CE96F+8 (2), 0CE9E1+4 (8), 0CEA11+4 (6).

- 67 of the 70 lists are reached from the table. Unreferenced: 0CE8E6 (scanline band $20 + dispatcher), 0CE9EA (palette bundles $01 and $32, dispatcher, scanline band $0F) and 0CEA45 (bundles $44 and $45 + dispatcher, a copy of 0CEA2F).
- The dispatcher is the last record in most lists but the first in some (for example 0CE8C7, 0CE959, 0CE98D, 0CE99A, 0CE9A3, 0CE9AC); the credits list 0CEA5B has none.
=== WHAT THE CODE FILES SAY ===

The block notes of ambient_palette_cycler, scanline_band_hdma_thinker and global_ambient_dispatcher describe the parameters. The 204 records are 59 ambient_palette_cycler, 59 global_ambient_dispatcher, 30 scanline_band_hdma_thinker and 56 spread over the other thinker code files. The list order is the spawn order. What each bundle or band looks like on screen was not traced.
Byte check: 1398 = 512 (256 pointers) + 204 x 4 (records) + 70 ($FF terminators). The ?INCLUDE list at the top names the 45 thinker code files the records point at.

scene_thinkers: 256 word pointers, index = scene ID. An entry may point into the middle of a list (the +4 / +8 suffix is the byte offset), see the block note.
thinker_spawn_0CE7E5: The bare list: only global_ambient_dispatcher. Used by 70 scenes.
thinker_spawn_0CE7EA: Shared default list: ambient_palette_cycler (bundle $3F), flag_gated_palette_cool, scanline_band_hdma_thinker (band $02), global_ambient_dispatcher. Entered at +0 by 2 scenes, at +4 by 4 and at +8 by 43.
thinker_spawn_0CE8E6: Unreferenced by the table: scanline_band_hdma_thinker band $20 and global_ambient_dispatcher (OQ-I072-3).
thinker_spawn_0CE9EA: Unreferenced by the table: palette bundles $01 and $32, global_ambient_dispatcher and scanline band $0F (OQ-I072-3).
thinker_spawn_0CEA45: Unreferenced by the table: a copy of thinker_spawn_0CEA2F (bundles $44 and $45 and the dispatcher) (OQ-I072-3).

blockNote: The console-string text of the menus (Bank 01, 121304-125711 = $01:D9D8): the boot and title strings, ten pointer tables and the loose strings between them, all drawn by ConsoleStringRenderer. It is read in two ways: RunBg3Script runs a loose string directly (a BG3 script), and the text tag [TBL:@table,addr] picks a table entry with a 16-bit RAM variable as the index (item_name_table by $0AC6, the other tables by $0AE8, character_name_table by $0AD4 and misc_ui_strings by $0B26). Text tags: [N] = line break of one tilemap row, [DBL] = two rows, [LU:n] = shared word n (shared_word_table), [POS:x,y] = cursor, [PAL:n] = palette, [RCC:w,h] = clear (w+1) x (h+1) tiles. The old note called the block 'all game UI text organized into 10 sub-tables'; the dialogue lines are DialogString data elsewhere, and seven of the ten part notes were wrong (see below).
=== TABLES (the index variable decides what the number means) ===
| Part | Bytes | Entries | Index | Content |

| consolestring_01D9D8 | 121304-121535 | 3 loose strings | | The region lockout warning (sFB_boot_logo, @system_strings.boot_screen_strings), then 'PUSH START BUTTON' and the copyright text (sFC_title_intro) |

| item_name_table | 121535-122398 | 64 | item ID ($0AC6 = equipped item) | The name with [N] line breaks for the two-row name areas (status screen: [TBL:@item_name_table,AC6] at (8C,3)). $00 empty, $29-$37 blank (8 spaces), $38-$3F 'Mystic Statue' |

| item_menu_table | 122398-123178 | 64 | item ID ($0AE8) | The same names on ONE line, printed as the first part of the item description box: [TBL item_menu_table][TBL item_description_table] (E9D0) and 'name, Discard?, No, Yes' (E9E2). $29-$37 blank, $38-$3F 'Mystery Doll' |
| non_discardable_item_bits | 123178-123186 | 8 bytes | item ID | Bit table: byte = ID >> 3, bit = BitMaskTable[ID & 7] (bit 0 = lowest ID of the byte); CheckItemDiscardable (inventory_menu) |

| item_description_table | 123186-124396 | 41 ($00-$28) | item ID ($0AE8) | Description text of two to four rows, each starting with [DBL] so it continues under the name; $00 = 'Nothing'. Items $29-$3F have no entry |
| ability_menu_table | 124396-124509 | 12 | ability index ($0AE8) | One-line ability name, header of the ability description box (EAB4) |
| ability_name_table | 124509-124636 | 12 | ability index ($0AE8) | The ability name with [N] line breaks, printed on the status rows (EA49, EA56, EA63) |
| ability_description_table | 124636-124878 | 13 ($00-$0C) | ability index ($0AE8) | Ability description text starting with [DBL]; $00 = 'Nothing' |
| character_name_table | 124878-125260 | 4 | characterForm ($0AD4) | ' Will', ' Freedan', ' Shadow' and ' Shadow' (form 3 repeats form 2), followed by 15 loose HUD and status-screen strings |
| misc_ui_strings | 125260-125711 | 2 | button layout ($0B26) | 'B' (layout 0 = Type 1) and 'Y' (layout 1 = Type 2), the item-use button name printed in E919; followed by 20 loose menu strings |

Ability index = characterForm x 4 + ability slot + 1 ($0AE8, ComputeAbilityIndex); entry 0 is the empty / 'Nothing' entry. Will: $01 Psycho Dash, $02 Psycho Slider, $03 Spin Dash, $04 empty; Freedan: $05 Dark Friar, $06 Aura Barrier, $07 Earthquaker, $08 empty; Shadow: $09-$0B are the placeholder strings DEFENCERK, DARKCOREK and BLACK4K (descriptions 'Dark 1' in $09-$0C), not real abilities.

Item IDs named here are the same IDs as in the chest table and the inventory icons: $01 Red Jewel, $02 Prison Key, $03-$04 Incan Statue A / B, $05 Incan Melody, $06 Herb, $07 Blue Block, $08 Wind Melody, $09 Lola's Melody, $0A Meat, $0B-$0C Mine Key A / B, $0D Memory Melody, $0E Crystal Ball, $0F Elevator Key, $10 Palace Key, $11 Purify Stone, $12 Statue of Hope, $13 Rama Statue, $14 Magic Dust, $15 Blue Journal, $16 Lance's Letter, $17 Necklace Stones, $18 Will, $19 Teapot, $1A Mushroom Drop, $1B Bag of Gold, $1C Black Glasses, $1D Gorgon Flower, $1E-$23 Hieroglyph (six), $24 Aura, $25 Lola's Letter, $26 Father's Journal, $27 Crystal Ring, $28 Red Apple.
=== NON-DISCARDABLE BITS ===

The bytes are $BC $FF $FF $FE $DF $00 $00 $00. Discardable (bit clear): $00, $01 Red Jewel, $06 Herb, $18 Will, $25 Lola's Letter, $28-$3F. Protected: $02-$05, $07-$17, $19-$24, $26 and $27. $18 and $25 being discardable is unexplained (OQ-I072-2).
=== WHAT WAS WRONG IN THE OLD NOTES ===

item_menu_table was 'longer descriptions shown when hovering': it is the one-line NAME (the description is item_description_table). The blank item range was given as $2A-$38 and the 'Mystic Statue' range as $39-$3F; they are $29-$37 and $38-$3F (8 statues, as the 8 'Mystery Doll' tags of shared_word_table say). item_description_table was 'multi-line descriptions of function and lore': it has 41 entries of short function text. non_discardable_item_bits was 'padding / alignment data between two tables'; it is read by CheckItemDiscardable. misc_ui_strings was 'status labels, save/load prompts, game over text': the table is just 'B' and 'Y' and the loose strings are inventory-menu prompts, tab titles and three screen labels (PAUSE, FORCE, the button legend). The old part notes of item_name_table (blank and statue ranges) and consolestring_01D9D8 ('displayed at boot': two of the three are title-screen strings) were also off. character_name_table was 'Will, Kara, Lance, Erik, Seth and other story characters': it holds the three player forms.
Byte check: the ten parts add up to 4407 bytes = 125711 - 121304. Part addresses are from blocks.json; the strings between the tables are listed in the part notes.

consolestring_01D9D8: 3 fixed strings, none of them printed by the menus: this one is the region lockout screen of sFB_boot_logo ('WARNING! This game pak is not designed for your SUPER FAMICOM or Super NES.' and the Enix line; a 50 Hz console never leaves it). The next two, consolestring_01DA47 'PUSH START BUTTON' and consolestring_01DA5E the copyright text, are drawn by sFC_title_intro (the copyright first). The names file calls address 121304 boot_screen_strings, the label sFB_boot_logo uses.
item_name_table: 64 pointers, index = item ID. The names carry [N] line breaks for the two-row status area; item_menu_table has the same names on one line. Empty at $00, blank (8 spaces) at $29-$37, 'Mystic Statue' at $38-$3F (the old note put the blank range at $2A-$38 and the statues at $39-$3F). $00 points at consolestring_01DB3F, the empty string shared with ability_menu_table and ability_name_table.
item_menu_table: 64 pointers, index = item ID. One-line item names: the first half of the item description box (consolestring_01E9D0 = this table + item_description_table) and the Discard? prompt (consolestring_01E9E2). It is not a table of descriptions. $29-$37 are blank and $38-$3F read 'Mystery Doll', unlike the 'Mystic Statue' of item_name_table (OQ-I072-1).
non_discardable_item_bits: 8 bytes $BC $FF $FF $FE $DF 0 0 0: one bit per item ID, set = cannot be discarded (byte = ID >> 3, bit = BitMaskTable[ID & 7]). Read by CheckItemDiscardable. Discardable: $00, $01, $06, $18, $25, $28-$3F.
item_description_table: 41 pointers ($00-$28), index = item ID; there is no entry for $29-$3F. Short descriptions of three or four rows, each starting with [DBL] so it continues below the name line; $00 = 'Nothing'.
ability_menu_table: 12 pointers, index = ability index (characterForm x 4 + slot + 1). One-line ability names; slots 4 of Will and Freedan are empty and the three Shadow entries are the placeholders DEFENCERK, DARKCOREK and BLACK4K.
ability_name_table: 12 pointers, index = ability index. The same names with [N] line breaks, printed after ':' on the status rows (consolestring_01EA49 / 01EA56 / 01EA63).
ability_description_table: 13 pointers ($00-$0C), index = ability index. $00 = 'Nothing'; $04 and $08 are empty; $09-$0C read 'Dark 1' (placeholders of the unused form-2 rows).
character_name_table: 4 pointers, index = characterForm ($0AD4): ' Will', ' Freedan', ' Shadow', ' Shadow' (form 3 repeats form 2; each name has a leading space). Used by the status screen (STYLE) and consolestring_01EA70 ('<name>'s cond.'). The part also holds the loose strings consolestring_01E7F6 to 01E919 (HUD, status screen and panel clears), see consolestring_01E7F6.
consolestring_01E7F6: HUD line redrawn by system_core: 5 raw tiles (ESC:1-5), the player HP bar [HP], the hundreds digit of DP ($0AD8, BCD) and the DP number ($0AD6). HudRedesign.patch.asm overrides it. consolestring_01E818 is the second HUD line (enemy bar [HE] with raw tiles 8-C, drawn by inventory_overlay and system_core). The six small strings consolestring_01E82B to 01E85C (digits 1-3 and raw tiles at (DE,1) / (9E,1)) have no label reference in the code or the patches (OQ-I072-3).
consolestring_01E870: Status-tab screen of the inventory: STYLE and the form name ([TBL:@character_name_table,AD4]), HP, DP, STR and DEF labels with their numbers, 'Items' with the equipped item name ([TBL:@item_name_table,AC6]) and the 'Dark Power' label (inventory_menu, the Status tab hover).
consolestring_01E919: 'Equipped. Equipment <B or Y> button to use.': the button letter comes from misc_ui_strings through [TBL:@misc_ui_strings,B26], the button layout of the save ($0B26).
misc_ui_strings: 2 pointers: 'B' and 'Y', index = button layout ($0B26: 0 = Type 1, 1 = Type 2). The part continues with the loose menu strings: the tab prompts ('Rearrange items.', 'Discard item.', 'Select item and enter.', 'Rearrange items? Select 1st item.', 'Select 2nd item.', 'Discard which item?'), the item and ability description boxes (consolestring_01E9D0, 01EAB4), the tab titles (Gather Items, Arrange Items, Discard Item, Dark Power), the ability rows (consolestring_01EA49 to 01EA63), the Status-tab hint (consolestring_01EA70), 'PAUSE' (consolestring_01EAC6, GlobalInputHandler), 'FORCE' (consolestring_01EAD1, radar_map_screen) and the button legend box (consolestring_01EADC, sFA_diary_menu).

=== HIDDEN GROUP ===

The 69 bytes after the 4-sub-sprite group 0F8BCC (header at 0F8BF5, 8 sub-sprites) are an extra group that no list points at: it is a byte-identical copy of the labelled group 0F8D7D. The extraction has no label for it and prints its 69 bytes as 10 more sub-sprites of 0F8BCC (rows ;04-;0D; only ;00-;03 are real), one byte too long. The same artefact is in spriteset_ability_fx (OQ-I067-5).
=== CHECKS ===

4325 bytes = 78 (39 pointers) + 39 x 2 + 164 x 4 (list terminators and records) + 63 x 13 (headers) + 385 x 7 (printed sub-sprites) - 1 (the overrun above). Whole-file counts; about 60% of the lines read (the table, all lists, the groups to 0F84EC, 0F87FD to 0F8864, 0F8B51 to 0F8C71, 0F8D1D to 0F8D7D and the last groups).
